scope: Frozen board hypotheses before classifier and fresh engine output. Source labels are nominations only. These judgments are narrow causal hypotheses, not an accuracy gold set.

cases.reason: Nh6+ vacates g4 for Qh5 and starts a kingside attack. The source line includes substantial Black counterplay; source interference does not yet identify a forced root mechanism.
checks: Enumerate Kh8 and capture replies, not only gxh6.
Do not transfer Black's later Ng3+/Nxf1+ counterplay to White's initiating move.
Compare mate/material liabilities before certifying clearance or interference.

cases.reason: Nb2 vacates c4 for Rc4+, while attacking Ra4. The checking rook then simultaneously attacks Kd4 and Bb4; the later fork belongs on Rc4, not automatically on the knight move.
checks: All rook escapes and bishop-saving replies must retain a connected payoff.
Remove Bb4: the quiet knight move must not borrow a now-absent rook-fork payoff.
Keep root preparation separate from the later checking fork.

cases.reason: Qg2+ offers several possible interpositions. On Qe4, Rd3+ deflects the king from defending that queen. That observed later deflection alone does not prove the root's primary mechanism.
checks: Enumerate all legal root interpositions, including rook/queen blocks.
Separate Qg2+ forcing preparation from actual Rd3+ king deflection.
Do not count a later queen capture twice or assume the source PV covers every defence.

cases.reason: Rxf2 offers the rook to Kxf2, after which Ne4 opens Qh4-f2 and also gives knight check. Acceptance geometry is clear; the full mating/material payoff and declines require proof.
checks: Enumerate declines and king flights before assigning forced attraction.
Ne4 is a later double/discovered check, not a current root arrow.
Debit the sacrificed rook and preserve counterchecks/material liabilities.

cases.reason: Qxf8+ draws Rf5 onto f8, then Rxf8+ forces the king toward h8=Q mate. A simultaneous attack on Bc8 is potentially incidental to that mating route.
checks: Independently enumerate every legal reply at both Black turns and verify final mate.
Remove Bc8 and check whether the same root still forces mate within the original distance; only then forbid its material-fork label.
Retain essential promotion and connected mating support rather than suppressing all compound motifs.

cases.reason: Bxe6 takes the attacking bishop before Qxc1 recaptures the other bishop. Immediate Qxc1 appears to allow Bxd5, losing the bishop that the intermediate exchange preserves.
checks: Compare Bxe6 with immediate Qxc1 and all Black counterchecks/declines.
The apparent e6-f7-g8 pin cannot itself prevent fxe6 from taking its attacker.
Credit retained material once, not a fresh capture at each later exchange.

cases.reason: e6+ attacks Kd7 and Nf7. The protected checking pawn cannot be captured by the king; source defensiveMove is not independently established.
checks: Enumerate every legal king reply and verify exf7 recovery with pawn-loss debit.
Determine whether a distinct immediate defensive necessity exists before crediting defensiveMove.
Keep the later Kxg5 collection connected and do not duplicate the knight payoff.

cases.reason: Bxg2 removes the dangerous pawn and brings the bishop onto the diagonal covering Nb7/Nc6 escapes of Na5; Bc7 attacks that knight, while Nd2/Pa2 cover other escapes.
checks: Enumerate knight escapes, counterchecks, guarding moves and attacks on Bc7.
Remove Nd2 and verify whether Nc4 becomes a safe escape; if so the trap must not survive unchanged.
Distinguish trapping the knight from merely taking the g2 pawn.

cases.reason: Nf3 develops without check, capture or an immediate two-target attack. Later pressure in the actual game is not root proof.
checks: Review engine alternatives separately; do not assume the actual continuation is best play.

cases.reason: a3 attacks Bb4, which can retreat to e7 or exchange on c3. Attacking one bishop is not itself a trap or fork; Bxc3 Qxc3 is not a free piece.
checks: Verify Be7's legality/safety and equal exchange accounting.
Do not attribute the later ...b5/Bxb5 pawn loss to a3.

cases.reason: a4 supports the bishop on b5 and attacks no enemy piece immediately. The later g4/Nxd4 exchange is a distinct event.
checks: Inspect strategic/defensive alternatives without treating missing proof as a positional certificate.

cases.reason: Bf4 develops and eyes the defended c7 pawn. The later Nb5/Nc7 sequence depends on subsequent moves and is not an immediate bishop fork.
checks: Keep the defended pawn attack separate from the later knight's opportunity.

cases.reason: a3 attacks Nb4 but Na6/Nc6 appear available. The actual ...Nxc2+ fork geometry is answerable by Qxc2 and must not alone prove a material win.
checks: Check both knight retreats and Qxc2 legal counterdefence.
Distinguish a conditional reply fork from a proved cause of White's pawn move.

cases.status: possible real mistake, not a quiet negative
cases.reason: Bd3 develops but leaves Bf4 attacked along Qc7-d6-e5-f4. The actual ...Qxf4 may win that bishop; whether Bd3 caused a missed saving duty needs comparison with alternatives.
checks: Verify the bishop is unprotected and Qxf4 has no tactical refutation.
Compare moves that save Bf4 before assigning a mistake cause.
Do not classify all six fixed contexts as positional just because they came from ordinary game plies.
